name.en: “Mum, I dropped my phone”: a new number asking for money

how.en: A text claims to be from your child or another family member. It says their phone was damaged and asks you to contact them on a new mobile number. If you reply, the scammer asks for bank account or credit card details, for example to buy a new phone. Just receiving the text does not put you at risk; replying does.

text.en: A text from an unknown number says it is your child or another relative.
They say their phone was damaged and give you a new number to use.
Once you reply, they ask for your bank account or card details to buy a new phone.
The money or card details go to the scammer.
Hi Mum, I dropped my phone and the screen is smashed. This is my temporary number, can you text me here? Need a favour x

en: text from my son new number
card details for a new phone
A relative writes from a new number saying their phone broke.
They ask for bank or card details, or money for a new phone.
They avoid a call on their usual number.
Don’t reply. Contact your relative on their regular number, or a close friend of theirs.
Forward the text free to 7726 (Department of Internal Affairs).
If you already paid, contact your bank straight away.

sources.title: “Mum I dropped my phone” SMS scam targeting New Zealanders
